title: Accessibility and string resources pass
findings_note: all UI strings hardcoded in MainScreen.kt; Icon(…, null) on reminder chip

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- Every user-visible string is hardcoded in Kotlin, which blocks F-Droid/Weblate translations and Play localization.
- Some icons have null descriptions in interactive contexts.
- Text-scaling and touch-target compliance haven't been checked.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - Compose UI test: `dashboard card exposes merged semantics label` (for example "Water, 2 of 8 glasses today, 5 day streak").

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Move all strings to `strings.xml`. Use `<plurals>` for streak, entry, and tracker counts, and `stringResource`/`pluralStringResource` in Compose. For VM messages, emit resource IDs and arguments in `UiEvent` rather than formatted strings.
2. Cards: apply `Modifier.semantics(mergeDescendants = true)` with a custom label. Quick-action buttons get an explicit `contentDescription` ("Mark Water done", "Add 1 to Water").
3. Verify that touch targets are at least 48dp, and that layouts still work at 200% font scale on a 360dp-wide device. Use `heightIn(min=…)` and avoid fixed `width(110.dp)`, which the old trend code had.
4. Run the Accessibility Scanner (Google, proprietary) or a TalkBack walkthrough manually. Record the results with `slicer note`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `./gradlew lintDebug` shows no `HardcodedText` or `ContentDescription` warnings, after enabling those checks.
- A TalkBack walkthrough of create, log, detail, and settings is completed.
